habitat: Rocky ground, and also stone walls and outbuildings on farms. It flicks its wings on landing.
summary: A common resident. A tame, nondescript small chat, recognised by repeated wing-flicking and a striking rufous or orange rump and tail. The southern and eastern races are darkest and largest. The tail is deep rufous. The Kemp name Familiar Chat and the code RB were left unchanged.

upperparts.pattern: The rump is rufous or orange. The tail is deep rufous.

viewNotes.note: Rufous or orange rump, and a deep rufous tail. It flicks its wings.

calls.description: Newman does not describe the voice. The grade A call is from Hillcrest. The filename is XC1009198-Chat_Familiar_LeDomaine_20250618_NR10.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. The rump is described as rufous or orange, so rufous is stored and the alternative is kept in the pattern. The voice is not described. The grade A call is from KwaZulu-Natal. The Kemp name Familiar Chat and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^7=128 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 64–256.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.
